---
title: "Recovery Checkpoint 2: Ready for Reusable R Workflows"
description: "A short optional recovery route after data import, tidying, and joins."
---

This checkpoint is for students who need to consolidate the first R phase
before writing more reusable workflows. It is not an extra assignment unless
the instructor says otherwise.

## Minimum Foundation

You should be able to:

- state the observation unit and identify a candidate key;
- inspect column names, types, dimensions, and missing values after import;
- use filtering, selection, mutation, grouping, and summarising intentionally;
- explain how a pivot changes the observation structure;
- predict whether a join can duplicate or drop rows;
- check parsing of strings, factors, and date-times;
- compare row counts and unmatched keys before and after a join.

## A 45-60 Minute Recovery Route

1. Run the [R setup check](../code/setup/check-r-setup.R).
2. Rerun the [Week 10 join audit](../code/r/week10-join-audit.R) and locate the
   checks for key uniqueness and unmatched records.
3. Complete core Exercises 1 and 4 from [Week 9](week-09-exercises.qmd) and
   Exercises 1, 3, and 6 from [Week 10](week-10-exercises.qmd).
4. For one table, write: “one row is…”, “the key is…”, and “a failed join would
   be visible because…”.

## Ready To Continue?

You are ready when you can import a table, state what one row means, explain a
join's expected cardinality, and name checks that would expose silent data
loss or duplication.
